title: Define SDK retry/timeout standard (RFC) + publish Confluence standard + ADRs
creator: Monica Patel
description:
Context
- We are seeing avoidable customer friction and support load from SDK inconsistencies: TS vs Python vs Go differ on retryable errors, max attempts, handling of Retry-After, and what “timeout” means (connect vs overall vs streaming).
- SRE flagged risk of “retry storms” during elevated 429s if we standardize poorly or ignore Retry-After.
- Security wants consistent guidance that does not increase secret exposure and avoids unsafe default logging.

Goal
- Draft a single standard for SDK retry/backoff + timeout semantics, collect SRE/PM/Security feedback, and publish:
  1) Confluence standard (implementation-level guidance)
  2) ADRs for retry policy + timeout model

Deliverables
1) RFC content that becomes a published Confluence standard:
   - Retryable status codes + network errors
   - Retry-After handling
   - Backoff algorithm + jitter
   - Max attempts defaults + caps
   - Budgeting (overall timeout interaction)
   - Streaming retry guidance (intentionally conservative)
   - Required logging/telemetry fields (where permitted)

2) ADRs (decision + rationale)
   - Retry policy v1 (defaults, configurability, streaming constraints, idempotency guidance)
   - Timeout model (overall vs connect/read, mapping to HTTP clients per language)

Proposed standard (v1)
A) Retry policy (non-streaming requests)
- Default: enabled for inference endpoints (POST) with conservative attempt limits.
- Retryable HTTP status codes:
  - 429 (rate limited): YES, but MUST respect Retry-After when present.
  - 500, 502, 503, 504: YES
  - 408: YES (request timeout)
  - 409: NO by default (can indicate conflict; avoid implicit retries)
  - 4xx other than 408: NO (including 400/401/403/404/422)
- Retryable network failures:
  - connection reset / ECONNRESET / broken pipe
  - TCP connect timeout
  - TLS handshake errors that indicate transient network failure
  - read timeout where no response bytes were received
  - DNS failures: NO by default (often configuration); can be opt-in via “retry_on_dns_error” if a language stack makes it hard to distinguish
- Max attempts (attempt = initial + retries):
  - Default max_attempts = 4 (1 initial + up to 3 retries)
  - Hard cap: 6 unless explicitly overridden with “unsafe_allow_high_attempts” (to prevent accidental thundering herd)
- Backoff:
  - Exponential backoff with jitter
  - Base delay: 250ms
  - Multiplier: 2.0
  - Max delay: 8s
  - Jitter: “full jitter” (uniform random between 0 and computed delay)
- Retry-After:
  - If present on 429/503, the client MUST sleep for max(retry_after, computed_backoff) with a cap of 30s (to avoid infinite waits and user confusion).
  - Parse both formats:
    - seconds (delta)
    - HTTP-date

B) Timeout model
- Standard defines three timeouts:
  1) connect_timeout_ms (time to establish connection)
  2) read_timeout_ms (idle time waiting for bytes after request is sent)
  3) overall_timeout_ms (wall-clock budget across attempts)
- Default values (non-streaming):
  - connect_timeout_ms = 10_000
  - read_timeout_ms = 60_000
  - overall_timeout_ms = 120_000 (budget across retries; each attempt must be bounded so retries don’t silently extend beyond overall)
- Default values (streaming):
  - connect_timeout_ms = 10_000
  - read_timeout_ms = 300_000 (idle timeout; resets on received bytes)
  - overall_timeout_ms = 0 (disabled) by default for streaming, but strongly recommended in docs to set per application (e.g., 10–30 min) to avoid hung connections
- Budgeting rule:
  - overall_timeout_ms is a hard budget; before each retry, check remaining budget. If remaining budget <= 0, do not retry; surface timeout.

C) Streaming semantics (retry guidance)
- Default: do NOT automatically retry after receiving any streamed tokens/events.
  - Rationale: once partial output is delivered, replaying the request can duplicate side effects (tool calls) and/or confuse application state.
- If stream disconnect happens before any tokens/events:
  - Treat as retryable if underlying failure is retryable AND attempt budget remains.
  - If retry occurs, surface “retry_count” and the final request_id.
- If disconnect happens after partial output:
  - Raise a typed StreamingInterruptedError including:
    - request_id (if known)
    - bytes_received / events_received (best-effort)
    - partial_output (best-effort)
    - retryable=false by default
  - Docs must recommend application-level patterns:
    - idempotency keys for tool calls / writes
    - prompt strategies for resuming (“continue from: …”) where appropriate

D) Error taxonomy hooks (required fields surfaced by SDK)
- All SDK errors should carry (where available):
  - request_id
  - status_code
  - error_code (string enum from API gateway)
  - retryable (boolean)
  - retry_after_ms (if parsed)
  - attempt / max_attempts
  - timeout_ms (effective)

E) Logging / telemetry (minimum)
- SDKs must provide either:
  - a hook/callback for structured logging, or
  - standardized fields emitted through existing logger facilities
- Standard fields (names are part of the parity contract):
  - request_id
  - sdk_language, sdk_version
  - attempt, max_attempts
  - retry_count
  - retry_reason (status_code | network_error | timeout)
  - retry_after_ms (if any)
  - timeout_connect_ms, timeout_read_ms, timeout_overall_ms
  - streaming_disconnect_reason (if streaming)

Non-goals (v1)
- Introducing new server-side idempotency features (we will document usage of existing idempotency header guidance; platform work tracked separately)
- Retrying tool/function calls automatically at the SDK layer beyond the HTTP request boundary
- Changing product semantics for how inference is billed; we only tighten client behavior and docs

Acceptance criteria
- Confluence standard published under Architecture & Standards
- ADRs merged/published (retry policy v1, timeout model)
- SRE + Security + PM sign-off recorded in this ticket
- Standard is specific enough that each language owner can implement without interpretation drift (includes exact default values and retryable conditions)
- Explicit section on streaming retry limitations + idempotency guidance

Links (published)
- Confluence Standard: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/sdk-retry-timeout-standard.json
- ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-sdk-retry-policy-v1.json
- ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-sdk-timeout-model.json

Rollout notes
- Must coordinate with platform gateway work to ensure Retry-After on 429 is consistent and request_id is always present (dependency ENG-5130).
- Monitor retry rate + 429s + p95 latency during beta rollout to avoid increased load.
comments: 2026-01-15 (Monica Patel): Creating P0 since this blocks implementation across all three SDKs. Please use this ticket as the single thread for decisions; language owners should not pick their own defaults independently.

2026-01-17 (Ibrahim Khan): Drafted initial RFC outline in Confluence and pulled in Allison (SRE), Marcus (Security), Henry (PM). Main open questions: (1) retry caps, (2) whether to default overall timeout for streaming, (3) DNS failure classification.

2026-01-19 (Allison Grant): +1 on full-jitter exponential backoff. Strongly recommend hard cap on max attempts to reduce herd risk. Also require Retry-After parsing for both delta-seconds and date formats; we’ve seen mixed gateway behavior historically.

2026-01-20 (Sean Gallagher): SRE signoff conditional on: (a) respect Retry-After, (b) cap sleep to avoid indefinite wait, (c) overall timeout budget prevents retries extending request time unbounded. Also recommend default max_attempts=4, not higher.

2026-01-21 (Henry Cho): PM concern: customers have reported TS retrying non-retryable 4xx leading to duplicate billing worries. Please explicitly call out which 4xx are never retried, and ensure docs say how to disable retries or set max_attempts=1.

2026-01-22 (Marcus Lin): Security notes: no auth tokens/keys in error messages; redact Authorization header in any debug logs. OK with adding request_id and retry_count as long as secrets are not included. Also suggest we avoid “retry on DNS” by default; DNS issues often indicate misconfig.

2026-01-24 (Ibrahim Khan): Updated draft with explicit retryable status codes and network failure categories. Added: no retries after streaming emits tokens; raise StreamingInterruptedError with request_id + partial output best-effort.
2026-01-28 (Ethan Park): Platform can ensure Retry-After on 429 consistently (tracking ENG-5130). Please ensure standard allows Retry-After on 503 too; we might add that later.
2026-01-31 (Ibrahim Khan): Incorporated final feedback. Published standard + ADRs. Remaining follow-ups moved to implementation tickets (ENG-5123/5124/5125/5126).
